commentary: Challenges Aristotelian orthodoxy: celestial bodies composed of incorruptible fifth element (aether). Avicenna allows universal hylomorphism (all things = matter + form). Pico adopts this to argue that heavens are not wholly separate from terrestrial realm, thus accessible to human knowledge and magical influence. Links celestial and terrestrial causality.

latin_incipit: In coelo est materia eiusdem rationis cum materia inferiorum.
charge: Aristotle and scholastic tradition held celestial bodies to be ontologically distinct, composed of aether, incorruptible.
defense: Avicenna's universal hylomorphism provides metaphysical framework for explaining celestial influence on terrestrial matters through shared material substrate. This legitimizes astrological and talismanic correspondences.

english_translation.text: There is in the heavens matter of the same kind as that of lower things.

exegesis: Pico's conclusion on Necessity within the Avicennism (Islamic Philosophy) tradition.
